episodes.157924: Thunderstorms developed along a strengthening low level jet across west central Wisconsin during the early morning of Thursday, June 17th. Ample elevated instability in an increasingly sheared environment allowed for a storm to become severe and produce quarter size hail in Dunn County, Wisconsin.
episodes.157940: During the late afternoon, and early evening of Thursday, June 17th, thunderstorms began to develop along an outflow boundary from earlier convection across far southern Minnesota. The storms developed in an area of ample instability and wind shear of 40 to 50 knots across southern Minnesota, and into west-central Wisconsin. The first storm developed across northwest Le Sueur County and moved east-northeast across southern Scott, and northern le Sueur County. The city of Lonsdale received hail that measured up to 2.5 inches in diameter. Other hail between an inch, and up to 2 inches in diameter fell along the Scott/Le Sueur County border, eastward toward northern Rice and southern Dakota Counties, and into Goodhue County. Some of the storms deviated well southeast across Goodhue County and produced the largest hailstones of 3 inches in diameter near Cannon Falls. Eventually, other storms developed across southern Minnesota, and moved eastward into west central Wisconsin.||There was an estimated 150 houses that were exposed to the 2 hail or greater. An estimate of 1,000 houses were exposed to 1.5 hail or greater. Based on total and partial roof replacement, the total damages to this hailstorm was approximately 5.5 million dollars.
episodes.157947: A broad ridge of high pressure aloft was anchored from the Four Corners Region east into the Southern Plains on June 17th. Meanwhile, an upper level disturbance rounded the ridge and drifted southwest across Western Arkansas and Southeast Oklahoma during the afternoon, over an area where moderate instability developed once temperatures climbed into the lower and mid 90s. Given the higher terrain over this area, orographic ascent helped to increase large scale forcing beneath this disturbance such that isolated showers and thunderstorms developed during the mid and late afternoon, and became severe as they entered Northern McCurtain County Oklahoma. Reports of quarter size hail and damaging winds which downed trees were received from this storm as it spread west, before entering Southern Pushmataha County.
episodes.157979: A dry downburst from a collapsing thunderstorm caused severe wind, blowing dust and reduced visibility at one of the ASOS's.
episodes.158033: Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon, and early evening across west-central Wisconsin, near Eau Claire. Other storms developed across southern Minnesota, and moved across west-central Wisconsin around Red Wing to Durand.
episodes.158034: A few isolated thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the late evening hours of the 16th. One of these storms passed over the Duluth area bringing a few reports of nickel-sized hail along with a lightning strike that hit a parked vehicle and caused extensive damage.
episodes.158104: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak warm front that extended southeast from a low pressure center over the central Plains. Hail and gusty winds accompanied the strongest storm.
episodes.158449: A cluster of thunderstorms developed over northwest to west central Iowa late in the evening of June 16th, strengthening on the nose of warm air advection and the low level jet. The initial discrete cell was able to produce up to ping pong balled sized hail. As the cluster developed further into a small bowing segment, damaging wind gusts became more prevalent.
episodes.158789: An unsettled weather pattern remained over South Florida with a mid-level trough producing cool temperatures aloft and southwesterly flow keeping sufficient tropical moisture across the region. As sea breeze boundaries developed, the flow favored a dominant Gulf breeze, which helped to develop thunderstorms over the east coast metro areas. A few storms were strong enough to produce gusty winds as they moved offshore the east coast.
episodes.158848: A surface front and drier air was settling southward across SE GA, with a differential heating boundary across NE FL near I-10 due to cirrus blow-off from storms in Appalachee Bay. Strong to severe storms formed across NE FL due to heating and interactions with the differential heating boundary and sea breezes.
episodes.158849: Sea breeze storms merged during the afternoon and evening. With slow storm motion < 10 kts, locally heavy rainfall cause brief flooding.
episodes.159133: Several rounds of storms moved across portions of southeast Minnesota on June 17th. Storms during the early morning hours dropped penny sized hail near Wykoff (Fillmore County). Much stronger storms occurred during the evening and dropped large hail across parts of Wabasha and Winona Counties. Hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter fell near Conception (Wabasha County) with two inch diameter hail falling near Kellogg (Wabasha County).
episodes.159838: As a cold front pushed into an environment of large MLCAPE (2000-3000 J/kg) and high DCAPE (1000 J/kg), scattered elevated thunderstorms developed on the nose of a 40 knot low-level jet across southwest Minnesota. These storms dropped south southeast through northwest Iowa during the evening producing periodic large hail and some damaging wind gusts as the low-level jet veered ahead of the advancing boundary.
episodes.159839: As a cold front pushed into an environment of large MLCAPE (2000-3000 J/kg) and high DCAPE (1000 J/kg), scattered elevated thunderstorms developed on the nose of a 40 knot low-level jet across southwest Minnesota. These storms dropped south southeast through northwest Iowa during the evening producing periodic large hail and some damaging wind gusts as the low-level jet veered ahead of the advancing boundary.
episodes.160107: Mid level moisture increased over northern Arizona and isolated thunderstorm developed. A landspout formed along a gust front from a thunderstorm.
episodes.160172: Mid level moisture increased over northern Arizona and isolated thunderstorm developed. A landspout formed along a gust front from a thunderstorm.
episodes.160627: A deep upper trough of low pressure extended down the eastern United States into the northeast Gulf of Mexico, with a deep cyclonic gyre in the Bay of Campeche.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developing over Cuba spread north and northeast, producing widespread gale-force wind gusts over the Florida Keys.
